questions.question: OP-01/O92 (AX-2, read(0)): 10 bytes remain on an Open stream; the caller calls read(0), then read(10). D6 has read(0) return b'' and also says the content is whole 'once b'' is returned', which cannot both hold. What does read(0) do with bytes remaining?

options.label: As io and D155 (Recommended)
options.description: read(0) returns b'', moves neither the position nor the state; on an Open stream that b'' is not the end. D6's end sentence reads 'once a read of nonzero size returns b''. The following read(10) returns all 10 bytes. Same rule as read1(0) in D155. Source: io.BufferedIOBase.read, D155.

options.label: Caller error
options.description: read(0) raises ValueError before any effect (D33, D51), state unchanged. Breaks io-contract code that probes with read(0), and differs from D155's read1(0) and empty-buffer readinto, which return b''/0.

questions.question: OP-01/O92 (AX-2, read(0)): 10 bytes remain on an Open stream; the caller calls read(0), then read(10). D6 has read(0) return b'' and also says the content is whole 'once b'' is returned', which cannot both hold. What does read(0) do with bytes remaining?

OP-01/O93 (AX-6, entry into Exhausted): a stream over a 10-byte item; read(10) returns all ten bytes; the next read(10) meets a stream-read failure (D96) or a cancellation. When does the stream enter Exhausted?

options.label: When its last byte goes out (Recommended)
options.description: Exhausted once the bytes delivered reach the content's length fixed at open (D22), so the next read returns b'' (D132) with no backend contact and fails only with a caller error; a cancellation still closes it (D50). Under E4 the end is the one a read meets (D26). Matches D18's labels and its 'starts Exhausted for an empty item'. Source: D18, D22; HTTP Content-Length.

options.label: When a read reports the end
options.description: Exhausted only once a read returns b'' (or 0, []); that read may need a backend request, so it can fail (Open → Failed, D16, D51) or be cancelled (Closed) after every byte arrived; a copyfileobj then fails with the whole content in hand. D18's 'starts Exhausted for an empty item' is withdrawn. Source: io.RawIOBase (0 bytes signals EOF).

options.label: Unspecified, either
options.description: F3 unspecified: the read after the last byte returns b'', or raises a stream-read failure (Failed), or is cancelled (Closed); a check accepts all three. Backends pick per transport. Weakest promise; tests cannot pin the state. Source: Go io.Reader (n bytes with EOF or nil).
